sources.sections_read: Lines 7–86; two sequence variables, collect/append, conditional collecting, destructive nconc distinction

sources.title: Bounding Self-Labeling Kubelets — API-based allowed-label configuration
sources.sections_read: Motivation; Proposal; Alternatives Considered / API-based configuration
sources.confirmed: The rejected alternative makes an API object control permitted labels. The stated counterargument is an escalation path if a compromised node can alter that object; it is distinct from file/flag configuration and a universally fixed allowlist.
sources.limits: The source does not name Gatekeeper and does not prove every admission-policy engine implements this alternative. Matching requires the retained candidate to apply API-managed policy to Node-label writes.

sources.title: SE0022 Objective-C selectors — type-safe calling-convention alternative
sources.sections_read: Alternatives considered: primary type-safe selector alternative; syntax alternatives

sources.title: Type-safe selectors — original proposal and design objections
sources.version_or_date: 2015-12-04 original discussion; live migrated forum rendering
sources.confirmed: The proposal attaches typed arguments and return values to selector references while retaining a selector-pointer representation; replies discuss ARC method families, receiver types, and target/action arity conflicts. The opening post reports inspiration from a D/Objective-C prototype, but the Swift alternative being proposed is the new calling convention.
sources.limits: The prototype is a cited inspiration inside the discussion, not the frozen gold identity S0022-G01. Its independent documentation was not opened here and its implementation is not newly verified.

sources.title: Property getter/setter exposure — full-property lens reply
sources.version_or_date: 2015-12-17 UTC reply 3; live migrated forum rendering
sources.confirmed: The reply proposes a full property interface, notionally T -> inout U, to preserve recursive writeback and efficient partial mutation for copy-on-write values. It distinguishes such a lens from separate getter/setter functions and does not name an external implementation or publication.
sources.limits: This is a proposed Swift property-access design; general use of the term lens elsewhere is insufficient to match its required semantics. The initial post-level URL failed, and this topic URL successfully exposed the relevant reply.
